content.title: About
content.content: A goose egg is a large egg laid by domestic or wild geese. When boiled (about 10‑12 minutes) the yolk becomes firm and the white turns rubbery. Goose eggs are nutrient‑dense and have a richer flavor than chicken eggs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Goose eggs are roughly 1.5‑2 times larger than chicken eggs.
They are often used in festive dishes and baked goods where a firmer texture is desired.
The yolk of a goose egg contains more vitamin A and D than a chicken egg yolk.
In some cultures goose eggs are considered a delicacy and are served in fine‑dining restaurants.
Chicken and goose eggs can be interchanged in recipes, but goose eggs require longer cooking times.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: One goose egg provides about 13 g of protein, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D is essential for bone health and immune function; goose eggs are one of the few food sources of this vitamin.

items.title: Contains vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, skin health, and immune response.

items.title: Minerals: iron and selenium
items.content: Iron aids oxygen transport, while selenium offers antioxidant protection.

items.title: Polyunsaturated fatty acids
items.content: Goose eggs provide omega‑3 and omega‑6 fatty acids, beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions, ranging from mild to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High cholesterol content
items.content: A single goose egg contains about 370 mg of cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol should limit intake.

items.title: Risk of salmonella
items.content: Like all eggs, goose eggs can carry salmonella; ensure they are fully cooked.

items.title: Large size
items.content: Because of their size, goose eggs can be a choking hazard for young children if not cut properly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled goose eggs can be eaten as a snack, sliced into salads, used in sandwiches, or added to baked goods for a denser crumb. They also pair well with sauces, herbs, or spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store boiled goose eggs in the refrigerator in a sealed container for up to 5‑7 days. Do not wash them before storage to avoid promoting bacterial growth.
